newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - MIM said re-rated after U.S. roadshow.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - MIM said re-rated after U.S. roadshow.

text.p: Shares in mining house MIM Holdings Ltd were keenly sought on Thursday as fund managers began a positive re-rating of the company, brokers said.

The head of one institutional dealing desk told Reuters that the rise in MIM's share price over the last few days and the large turnover was due to a United States roadshow presentation this week by MIM managing director Nick Stump.

The roadshow was sponsored by brokerage firm Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, which changed its name earlier this week from Bain and Co. MIM would not confirm Stump's visit, saying only that he was overseas and would return next Monday.

Another Sydney-based institutional broker said he was not aware of the roadshow and attributed the re-rating to the higher copper price and positive feedback from analysts who visited the core Mount Isa operations in northwest Queensland this week.
MIM topped the turnover list on Thursday with 17.69 million shares traded. Its shares were three cents higher at A$1.77 at 1.40 p.m. (0240 GMT), three cents off their day's high.

Stump said on November 14 that 1996/97 would be a difficult year for MIM with low metal prices and a strong Australian dollar. The emphasis this year would be on operating improvements and higher production, he said.
MIM achieved a net profit of A$170.6 million in 1995/96 (July/June) compared with a loss of A$216.1 million a year earlier.

The company said in its 1995/96 annual report that some major projects now under development would not contribute to earnings in the current year, namely the Alumbrera copper mine in Argentina, the majority-owned Ernest Henry copper/gold project in Queensland, and the Enterprise base metals mine near Mount Isa.
